minutes_text:
Arts Commission

  Inglewood, California
  July 16, 2025

A meeting of the Inglewood Arts Commission convened on July 16, 2025. Chairman
Jacques Lesure called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m., followed by the flag salute.

Ramara Rubin announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:
   Commissioner Aletha Metcalf - District 1
   Commissioner Olivia Alvitre - District 2
   Commissioner Phyllis Battle - District 3
   Commissioner Perryman-Banks - District 4
   Chairman Jacques Lesure - Commissioner at Large

City Personnel present were as follows:

   Kerri Arroyo  Library Director
   Ramara Rubin  Secretary

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None

MINUTES. Commissioner Metcalf moved, and Commissioner Battle seconded, that the
minutes for the Arts Commission meeting held on June 18, 2025 be approved.
The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
Ayes: Commissioners Metcalf, Alvitre, Lesure, Perryman-
Banks, and Battle
Noes: None
   Arts Commission

  VERBAL REPORTS-Public Art‐Related Projects.
  a. Helen Lessick, presented a midpoint report on the Experiments in Public Arts
  Project, which included artist-led workshops, a panel discussion, and a book
  launch marking the Anniversary of the Percent for the Arts Program.
  b. Kerri Arroyo, Library Director, provided an update on her experience at the
  American Library Association (ALA) Conference, the extended hours and
  additional day of service at the Crenshaw-Imperial Branch, the upcoming
  grand opening of the Morningside Library, and the Inglewood Public Library
  Summer Reading Program, which engaged over 300 patrons.
  c. Kerri Arroyo, Library Director, discussed various public art projects, including
  Self-Evident (for Sally Hemings) by Tori Ellison, Inglewood Genesis by June
  Edmonds, as well as the maintenance of the History of Transportation mural
  and Michael Massenburg’s Circle of Sounds.
  d. Kerri Arroyo, Library Director, reviewed the Public Art Fund balance,
  highlighting several pending and active projects. Jorge Gomez of The Money
  Studios shared an update on the Night Market Project, noting its
  postponement. Gomez will revisit the event in the next fiscal year, with the
  allocated budget carrying over.

PUBLIC REMARKS.
  a. Jorge Gomez announced a community art gathering at Asteroid Vinyl Café on
  July 19, 2025, from 2:00 to 6:00 p.m.
  b. Joyce Dallal of Inglewood Open Studios (IOS) mentioned the opening of
  applications for the Willie Stoffer Visual Artist Grant, which will close on
  September 15, 2025.
  c. Commissioner Metcalf shared her positive experience at the Willie Stoffer
  Visual Art Exhibition held at the Inglewood Public Library in collaboration
  with Inglewood Open Studios on May 24, 2025.
   Arts Commission

COMMISSIONERS’ COMMENTS/INITIATIVES/ART CALENDAR.
  a. Commissioner Metcalf invited the public to Councilwoman Gloria Gray’s
  District 1 Family Unity Day event, scheduled for Saturday, July 26, 2025,
  from 12:00 to 5:00 p.m.
  b. Chairman Lesure shared highlights of his trip to Kenya and reflected on the
  positive experience.
  c. Commissioner Perryman-Banks thanked the audience for their participation
  in the Arts Commission meetings.
Chairman Lesure moved, and Commissioner Perryman-Banks seconded, to postpone the
August Arts Commission meeting to September 17, 2025, at 6:30 p.m.
The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
Ayes: Commissioners Metcalf, Alvitre, Lesure, Perryman-Banks, and Battle
Noes: None

There being no further business to be presented, Chairman Lesure declared the meeting
adjourned at 7:11 p.m.
